evidence.label: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow on projective space

headline: Claims a smooth starting metric on complex projective 10-space whose Calabi flow breaks down in finite time.
scope: Calabi flow from one smooth U(10)-invariant Kähler metric in the Fubini–Study class of CP¹⁰, and its products with constant-scalar-curvature factors.
plain: Calabi flow is an equation that slowly reshapes a curved complex space, aiming to make its curvature even. Chen conjectured that it runs forever from any smooth start. The paper claims a smooth start on complex projective 10-space where the curvature becomes infinite at one point in finite time. The space even carries a perfectly even metric, so the failure is not caused by the space itself. There is no Lean check.
doesNot: This does not show that weak versions of the flow fail, and it says nothing about complex dimensions below ten. It has no Lean check.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Eugenio Calabi, who introduced the flow
scorecard.significanceWhy: It claims to disprove a standing conjecture of Chen on smooth long-time existence for Calabi flow.

explanation:
Start with complex projective space of dimension 10, CP¹⁰. It is the set of complex lines through the origin in an 11-dimensional complex space. It carries a standard symmetric metric, the Fubini–Study metric. Scalar curvature is one number at each point that averages all the bending there. With the paper's normalization, Fubini–Study has scalar curvature 110 at every point. That is 10 × 11, the dimension times one more.

A Kähler metric is a way to measure lengths on a complex space that fits its complex structure. Calabi flow changes such a metric over time. Where scalar curvature is above average it pushes one way, and below average the other. Calabi introduced it to find the most even metric in a family[1]. Chen conjectured that the flow runs smoothly forever from any smooth start[2]. On surfaces of complex dimension one this was known: Chruściel proved the flow lasts forever and settles down[3]. In higher dimensions the flow was known to continue while scalar curvature stays bounded[4].

The paper claims a no. It builds a smooth starting metric on CP¹⁰, in the same family as Fubini–Study[5]. The flow stops at a finite time T*. At one point p the scalar curvature grows like a constant times 1/√(T* − t)[5]. So when the time left falls from 0.01 to 0.0001, the curvature there grows about tenfold. Because the family contains the even Fubini–Study metric, the failure happens even where a perfect target exists[6]. Taking products with a fixed even factor gives the same breakdown in every complex dimension of at least 10[7].

How does the construction work? The metric is symmetric under a large group, U(10), so the flow reduces to one equation in one variable. At p the scalar curvature equals 110 times one minus a single value H(t,0)[8]. The paper builds an exact shrinking solution of a simpler flat model equation[9]. A computer calculation with exact arithmetic checks the matching inequalities for that solution[10]. The hard step is the correction on the compact space. It must stay smaller than the main term at p, so the blow-up survives[11]. The starting metric is chosen at the end, as a time slice of the solution[12].

How sure is this? There is no Lean check. A computer proof checker has not looked at the analysis. The profile step relies on a computer certificate that the paper includes. No specialist review of the paper has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if the construction holds: it would disprove Chen's long-time existence conjecture for Calabi flow. There is no Lean check, part of the proof is a computer certificate, and no specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: A way to measure lengths on a complex space that fits its complex structure.
An equation that changes a Kähler metric over time to even out its scalar curvature.
One number at each point that averages all the ways the space bends there.
The space of complex lines through the origin; CP¹⁰ has complex dimension 10.
The standard, fully symmetric metric on complex projective space; its scalar curvature is constant.
The family of Kähler metrics that differ by a smooth potential function; the flow stays inside one class.
A time at which the flow cannot continue smoothly because curvature becomes infinite.
